A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JailBound study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and support a complete comparison despite different pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original white-box and black-box attack experiments, loss ablations, and appendix experiments on latent knowledge and classifier configurations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 3–4 and the analyses in Figures 3–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same layer-wise logistic-regression probing, three loss components, and alternating image-perturbation and text-token updates. Removing Algorithm 1's reference to Equation 3 does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MM-SafetyBench's 13 safety categories and retain the same multimodal attack scenarios. Appendix A.1's contrastive-pair safety-classification experiment is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain the same modality-based comparison configurations. Figure 3 and Table 4 retain Baseline, UMK, FigStep, VAJM, and JailBound, with no comparator added or removed.

E3.justification: Both report the same 1,719-example benchmark, six evaluated VLMs, optimization settings, and evaluation procedures. The refusal-template ASR scoring and human/GPT semantic evaluation in Appendix A.4 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablations, semantic-preservation analysis, and Figure 5 case study are retained unchanged. Appendices A.1–A.3 preserve the same latent-knowledge, layer-training, and classifier-configuration analyses.

E5.justification: Point-estimate reporting and the annotation-agreement procedures in Appendix A.4.2 are unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 match entry for entry. Overall white-box ASRs remain 94.38%, 91.40%, and 97.19%; black-box ASRs remain 75.24%, 70.06%, and 56.55%, respectively in table model order. The plotted results and qualitative findings in Figures 3–8 also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and Appendix A.1's contrast-consistent learning objectives and inference definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about exploiting latent safety boundaries, jointly perturbing both modalities, and achieving strong white-box effectiveness and black-box transferability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of architectural sensitivity, shared multimodal vulnerabilities, semantic-preservation tradeoffs, and deeper-layer safety representations are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning unexplored defenses and fixed perturbation budgets.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same hyperparameters, learning rates, 20-token suffix, 8/255 visual perturbation bound, 100–150 iterations, and eight A100 GPUs. Appendix rejection templates, annotation instructions, and the evaluator prompt are unchanged; no resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The same 37 bibliography entries and research-positioning discussion are retained. Converting numbered citations to author–year citations does not add cited work or change the relationship to ELK, CCS, SCAV, or prior multimodal attacks.

P1.justification: v3 updates author affiliations and adds internship and corresponding-author notes, converts citations to author–year style, and removes Algorithm 1's equation cross-reference. The narrative and section order remain unchanged; some converted citations introduce duplicated author names.

P2.justification: The author block and citation formatting cause text and display reflow. Figures 3–4 shift within page 9, and Figure 5 moves from page 9 to page 10. All eight figures and six tables retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations, including the complete appendix content. Author-credit updates and citation/layout edits have small presentation tradeoffs, including awkward duplicated citations, but establish no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
